story.title: How I got here
story.lead: From a menu for a game to a product of my own: nine chapters on how I became a design engineer.

omsk.title: It started with a menu for a game
omsk.school: A maths and physics class. We wrote websites in Notepad, in plain HTML, CSS and JS: they taught us the hard way. From the seventh grade I lived in Photoshop, then found Illustrator, and in the eleventh, Figma.
omsk.game: In it I built a menu for a game I played all the time and posted it in the game's groups. People asked how to install it. It reached the developers: they offered me work, then opened my file and stopped answering.
omsk.quote: Over a hundred frames. Not one component.
omsk.after: I was furious at the time. Now I understand them.
omsk.menus: The Figma file of the game menu: dozens of nearly identical screens

university.title: Maths first
university.choice: I wanted to study product design, but a teacher talked me out of it: get your maths up first. So I ended up at Omsk State University, in applied mathematics and computer science.
university.roles: I always had top marks in programming, and in group projects I always ended up as the designer.
university.quote: It's a pain to check my own class schedule.
university.idea: Some universities had apps for that. From 2023 Maxim, a classmate of mine, and I kept talking about building one for ours, and kept putting it off: the idea felt too big.

build.title: VCourse
build.start: In our third year we were given a semester to build a product of our own, and neural networks had just grown up enough. We went for it. I took product design and the front end, Maxim the back end and DevOps.
build.learn: I had no experience in mobile development at all. The first semester went on Swift, SwiftUI, Xcode and Apple's guidelines.
build.quote: By the end of the semester my own app was on my phone.
build.polish: The next semester and the summer went on polish. The app was rewritten from scratch several times: I wanted it perfect.
build.screen: The university picker in the VCourse app

launch.title: Launch
launch.post: We agreed with the university on a post in its Telegram channel. The post went out, and we sat refreshing the pages, watching the numbers.
launch.quote: I had never felt anything that good.
launch.rankLabel: place among education apps on the Russian App Store, September 2025
launch.chart: App Store downloads per day, 1–14 September 2025
launch.chartSummary: 632 downloads in the first three days, 411 of them on 2 September. Source: App Store Connect.
launch.next: Over the next semester came Android and the website, and five more colleges and universities joined.
launch.eveCaption: 31 August 2025. The post goes out tomorrow

fork.title: The fork
fork.question: The app worked, and the question came up: what next? We couldn't keep growing it seriously and earn nothing from it.
fork.quote: Ads in the app, or a service for universities.
fork.answer: We really didn't want ads. We took the second road: our own service for building timetables, with the apps as a pleasant extra for students and teachers. We started talking to the people who make the timetables and took apart how it's really done.

night.title: One night
night.letter: My bachelor's was ending and I was looking at master's programmes in Omsk. One night a newsletter from Central University arrived: a programme in Human Experience Design. Literally what I had wanted to study from the start.
night.need: They asked for a portfolio. I didn't have one.
night.quote: I decided not to sleep until I had built something worth sending.

assets.subject: assets: add portrait and product screenshots

night.wait: The site went up on Vercel and the application went out. Then a call, and several weeks of silence.
night.grant: And then a letter: the largest grant they give.
night.move: One letter changed the plan: I was moving to Moscow.

rent.quote: …and now I had to pay for a flat somehow

moscow.title: Ten prompts
moscow.job: I moved at the end of the summer and started work: several iOS app designs a week, plus their ASO. Doing that by hand would have driven me mad.
moscow.agents: I tried agents in Figma. That took a whole pipeline, and it worked.
moscow.quote: I got a personal designer, and I became the boss.
moscow.prompts: I won't claim a complete app, with icons and an App Store page, comes out of one prompt. I will claim it comes out of ten thoughtful, consecutive ones.

now.title: Still going
now.first: VCourse keeps running: in September 2026 an average of 1,049 people a day used it, and new installs come by word of mouth.
now.firstSource: The app's API log, as of 4 October 2026
now.next: The next version is Pora na paru. I wrote new apps from scratch: the old foundation would have broken within a year. Now I'm building the web client and the timetabling service, and doing my master's.
now.quote: I have plenty of components now.
